title: Transition from the Episode of Emperor Karon to the Lineage of the Sikh Gurus

blocks.text: This page continues the criticism of corrupted storytelling by arguing that later writers had confused sakhi with gosht and mixed chronology with legend. The complaint is not minor, because it affects how readers understand what belongs to Guru Nanak, what belongs to older prophecy, and what belongs to careless retelling.

After exposing that confusion, the book turns toward firmer ground by opening the lineage of the Sikh Gurus. The movement from disputed anecdote to ordered succession gives the reader a more stable framework for sacred history.
In that sense the page is editorial even within the original text itself. It rejects muddle, then prepares the careful sequence of Gurus that follows.
